input: Research Tesla (tesla.com) for a hedge fund

catalysts.claim: Annual meeting on Dec 3, 2026 at 3:00 pm CT (record date Oct 13). Shareholders vote to re-elect Musk, Denholm and Straubel for 3-year terms, cast a non-binding say-on-pay vote on 2025 pay, and ratify PwC. There are no shareholder proposals and no Tesla merger item.

Possible Tesla–SpaceX merger. On SpaceX's Oct 20 call, Musk said both companies have special committees of independent directors studying a deal, but no terms have been agreed. Polymarket (cited Oct 29) priced an announcement at 19% by Dec 31, 2026 and 59% by Jun 30, 2027.

Barclays said a merger announcement could come before the AGM, flagging late Oct or early Nov 2026 as a likely window. As of Nov 4 nothing had been announced or filed. Barclays expects an announcement within 6–12 months.

Cybercab: on the Q3 call, Tesla said expansion beyond Austin starts in Dallas in November 2026 and reaches other cities by year-end. It also plans to start selling Cybercabs to fleet operators by end-2026. Musk said robotaxi won't show up in the financials until Q2 2027.
Sales restrictions on Tesla's SpaceX equity stake (fair value $2.865B at Sep 30, 2026), which date from SpaceX's IPO, expire in December 2026.

Musk said Gigafactory Texas will start winding down Cybertruck production around mid-2027 to make room for Cybercab. Shares rose 5.3% intraday on Nov 9 to about $381.01. Tesla is refunding some Cybertruck deposits.

Tesla's China promotion cuts the minimum down payment on 5-year interest-free loans for some Model 3/Y variants to 39,900 yuan (about 50% lower). It covers orders from Oct 30 to Nov 30, 2026, so November and December China data will show whether it worked.

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q3 2026 (reported Oct 21): revenue $28.05B, flat y/y and in line with the ~$28.06B consensus. Non-GAAP EPS $0.48 beat the $0.45 consensus but was down from $0.50. GAAP net income $787M ($0.22/share), down 43%.
A second source puts consensus higher: revenue of $28.441B (a 1.39% miss) and EPS of $0.4358 (a 10% beat).

Q3 margins: total gross margin 19.6% (16.8% in Q2, 18.0% a year earlier). Tariff refunds added a net $447M to gross profit. Operating margin was 2.6% and operating income $718M, down 56% y/y, as opex rose 39% to $4.78B, with R&D up 69% to $2.76B.

Q3 auto gross margin excluding credits was 18.1% (16.3% in Q2, 19.2% in Q1). FCF was $1.53B versus $3.99B a year earlier. Energy deployments of 13.7 GWh missed the ~15.9 GWh consensus. Management said battery availability was the limit on auto volumes.
Q3 deliveries were 486,532 against Tesla's company-compiled consensus of 461,974 (about 5% beat). Production was 464,391.

Current guidance: no formal revenue, EPS or volume guidance. Capex guidance is unclear. Electrek says the Q3 letter left 2026 capex at 'more than $25B', which would need about $12B in Q4. Money365 says the Q3 10-Q says 'more than $20B' and that the CFO said about $20B on the call. 9M capex was $13.01B. Management said opex will keep rising sequentially.
Active FSD subscriptions, including upfront purchases, reached 1.74M (up 67%). Cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles were nearly 2M.

Musk described a goal of about 5M vehicles a year by around 2030, calling it a goal rather than a forecast. Optimus production started on high-volume lines in Fremont, with a 'shallow slope' and 'somewhat bumpy' early ramp. Semi volume production started in Nevada.

event_driven.claim: Tesla–SpaceX combination: special committees have formed at both companies, with no terms or premium offered. Musk says a deal needs 50% of all Tesla shares outstanding, about 1.98B votes out of 3,952,757,946 shares, which he called 'quite a high hurdle.' J.P. Morgan (via investingLive) expects a SpaceX-led all-stock deal at a 30–35% premium.

After Democrats won the House and Senate on Nov 3, Deutsche Bank warned that regulatory scrutiny could block a Musk-promoted SpaceX–Tesla merger. Tesla and SpaceX lost about $456B in combined market value in two sessions, and Tesla fell about 11% intraday on Nov 5.

No buybacks reported. Common shares outstanding rose to 3,953M, mainly from equity awards and acquisitions. In Q2 2026 Tesla bought a 'Super Intelligence' hardware company for $1.95B in stock and equity awards, of which $1.73B depends on service or performance conditions.

Retail voting: the SEC cleared a retail auto-vote program on Sep 29, 2026. Per Tesla's SEC letter, retail holders voted only 28% of their shares in 2025, against 76.6% for institutions. That matters for any merger vote.

credit_signals.claim: Liquidity at Sep 30, 2026: $45.447B in cash, equivalents and short-term investments ($17.853B cash, $27.594B short-term investments). Recourse debt was only $2M. The $20B term loan (Sep 2029) and $10B revolvers (Sep 2027–Sep 2031) were undrawn.

Debt maturities: non-recourse debt is $1.311B current and $7.954B long-term. It includes a $5.966B China working capital facility maturing Oct 2026–Sep 2027. Automotive ABS runs to 2035 and energy ABS to 2050–2052.
Moody's affirmed Tesla at Baa3, stable, and gave SpaceX a first-time Baa1, two notches higher. Musk posted that 'Tesla's credit rating is ridiculously low.'
Cash burn has risen: 9M 2026 capex was $13.01B versus $6.13B a year earlier. Construction in progress includes $10.96B of AI ('SI') infrastructure. Trailing-twelve-month FCF is $3.30B.
Accrued warranty grew to $10.14B from $8.61B at year-end 2025. Regulatory credit revenue fell to $113M from $417M, after a $475M reversal for credits that had to be contractually returned.

alternative_signals.claim: China, October 2026: domestic retail sales were 8,817, down 66.1% y/y and the lowest since July 2022. Exports were 59,012, up 66.3%. Wholesale was 67,829, up 10.3% y/y but down 28.9% m/m. Tesla's China NEV retail share fell to 0.80% from 2.03%. Year to date, China retail is down 15%.
Europe, October 2026 registrations: Spain +271% (1,459 units), Sweden +248%, Norway +131% (1,548 units, best October on record, 9.8% share), France +35%, Denmark +34%.

Product mix: Musk said Cybertruck production in Texas winds down around mid-2027 to free up Cybercab capacity. Tesla sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in 2025, down from 38,965 in 2024. The base AWD trim was dropped, and Australia/NZ reservations were refunded.
Pricing: in October Tesla offered almost $3,000 off Model Y inventory in Australia, its latest price cut there.

Demand and pricing from the Q3 letter: Tesla reported its largest passenger-vehicle backlog in four years, but average selling prices fell again. Q3 deliveries exceeded production by about 22,000 units, and inventory was about 11 days of supply.

Robotaxi scale: Tesla runs small Model Y fleets in Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa. Waymo has more than 4,000 vehicles in over a dozen cities. Tesla changed its disclosed metric from 'paid' to 'unsupervised' robotaxi miles after Q2 paid miles fell 36% q/q.

insider_and_ownership.claim: CFO Vaibhav Taneja had 6,539 RSUs vest on Sep 5, 2026. On Sep 8, 2,605.75 shares were sold at $360.134 to cover tax withholding (issuer-automated, not a discretionary sale). He holds 25,972 shares directly and 111,000 in GRATs.
Musk holds about 20% of Tesla (per Khaleej Times) and more than 80% of SpaceX voting power.

Proxy: Musk's 2025 CEO Performance Award has 12 tranches, each tied to market-cap and operating milestones. None were earned or vested as of the proxy. The 2026 proxy lists about $158.4B of 2025 stock awards for Musk, and the 2025 interim award was forfeited in 2026.
Sell-side moves: Barclays upgraded to Overweight with a $450 target (from $370) on Oct 26. Tesla traded at $402.60 on Oct 29.

risks.claim: Earnings quality: Q3 operating margin was only 2.6%. The gross margin beat was helped by a $447M net tariff refund that may not recur, while R&D rose 69% y/y and management guided opex higher.
China domestic demand is weak: October retail fell 66% y/y to 8,817 units, the fifth straight y/y decline, and fell faster than China's NEV market (-13.7%).

Political and regulatory risk: Democrats now control Congress and the Texas governorship. The new Texas governor-elect has called for a moratorium on new data-center approvals, which could delay the Tesla/SpaceX 'Terafab' in Grimes County. Investors also expect probes into Musk's companies.

Autonomy regulation: NHTSA opened a probe in Sep 2026 into whether the Cybercab (no brake pedal or side mirrors) meets federal safety standards. A rule change removing those requirements is likely months away. Tesla's autonomy head said bottlenecks are also technical.
NHTSA opened a preliminary review on Oct 9, 2026 of a petition alleging Tesla robotaxis (about 1,000 2026 Model Y/Cybercab vehicles) sped in school zones.

Litigation: Judge Bloom (S.D. Fla.) refused to overturn the $243M Autopilot verdict, which includes $200M in punitive damages, with Tesla found 33% at fault. Tesla is expected to appeal to the Eleventh Circuit, so the precedent risk for other Autopilot/FSD cases remains.

Execution and capex: 2026 capex guidance has moved from >$20B to >$25B and back to about $20B. Q3 FCF fell 62% y/y to $1.53B, and trailing-twelve-month FCF is only $3.30B against a valuation built on AI and robotics.
Dilution and governance: a merger with SpaceX would be a related-party deal with Musk on both sides. He has said he is conflicted and stays out of the special committees' talks.

output.research_view: TSLA trades on two things that are hard to model: whether a SpaceX merger happens, and how fast Cybercab and robotaxi scale. The core business is weakening. Q3 operating margin was 2.6% with help from a one-off tariff refund, opex is up 39%, China retail is at a four-year low, and capex/FCF guidance has been unclear. The setup into year-end turns on the Dec 3 AGM, any merger announcement from the special committees (the Democratic Congress and Texas wins have raised the regulatory bar), the Dallas Cybercab launch and NHTSA's Cybercab standards review, and the December expiry of sales restrictions on Tesla's SpaceX stake. The balance sheet ($45B cash, almost no recourse debt, $30B undrawn) limits downside on credit, but not on the multiple.
